results.title: PT Indofood Sukses Makmur Tbk (INDF) highlighted as a cheap big-cap stock with low PE
results.body: The article focuses on PT Indofood Sukses Makmur Tbk (INDF), the Grup Salim issuer controlled by Anthoni Salim, being a low-priced big-cap stock. It notes that INDF trades at a trailing-twelve-month price-to-earnings ratio of 6.19× and closed at Rp 6,750, down 2.8% on 25 Sept 2026, with a weekly decline of 3.9% and a month-to-date drop of 8.4% while YTD it is only 0.3% lower. Financially, INDF posted Q2‑2026 revenue of Rp 31.6 trillion (‑6.7% QoQ, +11.8% YoY) and cumulative H1‑2026 revenue of Rp 65.5 trillion (+9.5% YoY); core profit fell 8.5% QoQ to Rp 3.1 trillion but rose 26% YoY, leading to H1 core profit of Rp 6.4 trillion (+6.9% YoY). Net profit declined 33.1% YoY to Rp 4.7 trillion, driven by a foreign‑exchange loss of Rp 3.4 trillion versus Rp 231 million a year earlier.

results.title: PT Sepatu Bata Tbk (BATA) President Director Amitav Nandy Resigns After One Year
results.body: PT Sepatu Bata Tbk (BATA) announced the resignation of its President Director Amitav Nandy after serving exactly one year. The resignation letter was received on 23 September 2026 and the decision will be taken at the upcoming shareholders meeting in accordance with OJK Regulation No. 33/2014. Amitav Nandy was appointed at the extraordinary general meeting on 25 September 2025, when shareholders also approved the closure of the Purwakarta shoe factory and the removal of the domestic shoe production line. Consequently, Bata will no longer produce shoes in Indonesia, focusing on its retail operations.

results.title: Bank Indonesia Holds BI‑Rate at 5.75% as Deposit Rates Remain Prone to Further Increases
results.body: Bank Indonesia decided to keep the BI‑Rate at 5.75%, leaving deposit rates across the banking sector still susceptible to upward movement through the end of 2026. CIMB Niaga reported a 10.03% year‑on‑year rise in cost of funds to Rp 5.73 trillion and a 0.06% decline in net interest income to Rp 6.93 trillion, while deposit rates for one‑month, three‑month and six‑month tenors rose to 5.1%, 5.8% and 5.6% respectively; OK Bank said its pricing follows industry trends and may become more selective, and Bank Tabungan Negara (BTN) indicated a recent lowering of its deposit rates.

results.title: PT Bank Danamon Indonesia Tbk (BDMN) reports consolidated LDR of 127% due to subsidiary funding structure
results.body: PT Bank Danamon Indonesia Tbk (BDMN) said its consolidated Loan-to-Deposit Ratio reached 127% and attributed the level to the funding structure of its subsidiaries. Fitch Ratings noted that the high LDR reflects borrowings used by subsidiaries PT Adira Dinamika Multi Finance Tbk and Home Credit Indonesia, with additional funding access from MUFG as Danamon’s parent. As of June 2026, Danamon’s consolidated credit and trade finance grew 12% year‑on‑year while customer deposits grew 14% year‑on‑year, and Fitch retained the bank’s national AAA rating with a stable outlook and a BBB long‑term issuer default rating.

results.title: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BRI) net profit rises 6.6% to Rp 34.77 trillion through August 2026
results.body: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BRI) reported net profit of Rp 34.77 trillion for the period ending August 2026, a 6.63% year‑on‑year increase from Rp 32.61 trillion. The profit growth was supported by a 3.44% rise in net interest income to Rp 77.26 trillion, higher commission and fee income of Rp 14.06 trillion, a 43.73% jump in dividend income to Rp 4.54 trillion, while interest expense fell 6.70% to Rp 32.41 trillion; loans expanded 13.66% to Rp 1,446.98 trillion, total assets grew 10.53% to Rp 2,127.78 trillion and the loan‑to‑deposit ratio reached 87.39%.

results.title: Foreign investors' net selling makes ten stocks, including PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI), PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBNI) and PT Bumi Resources Tbk (BUMI), top losers as the IHSG falls
results.body: Foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp559 billion on Friday, 25 September 2026, making ten stocks the largest foreign outflow victims while the IHSG weakened by 56.7 points (0.9%) to 6,241.8 at market close. Net sell in the regular market amounted to Rp440.3 billion and Rp118.7 billion in the negotiation and cash markets, with total transaction value reaching Rp9.3 trillion. The biggest foreign sell-offs were PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) with Rp62.8 billion, PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBNI) with Rp37.8 billion, PT Bumi Resources Tbk (BUMI) with Rp29.2 billion, TLKM with Rp112.7 billion and PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk with Rp71 billion. Overall, 122 stocks rose, 587 fell and 254 remained unchanged during the session.

results.title: BMRI and BBNI flagged as cheap stocks by BRI Danareksa
results.body: PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) and PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (BBNI) are highlighted as cheap big‑cap stocks, with trailing‑twelve‑months PE ratios of 6.1× and 6.3× respectively, closing at Rp 4,080 (+0.25%) and Rp 3,500 (‑0.5%) on 25 Sep 2026 and having slipped about 4 % over the prior week. BRI Danareksa Sekuritas also maintains an overweight view on the banking sector, recommends PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) as the top pick due to a solid net interest margin and a roughly 50 % savings‑account share, and projects aggregate bank net‑profit growth of 4 % annually in 2026, down from 11 % in H1 2026.

results.title: PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (MDKA) records largest foreign net buy as market sells intensify
results.body: PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (MDKA), an issuer owned by Edwin Soeryadjaya and Winato Kartono, recorded the largest foreign net purchase of Rp 76.8 billion during 21‑25 September 2026 while the Indonesian market posted a total foreign net sell of Rp 3.1 trillion. The net buying made MDKA the top‑ranked stock, ahead of PT Triputra Agro Persada Tbk (TAPG), which attracted a foreign net buy of Rp 70.1 billion and is owned by TP Rachmat LR Imanto and Meity Subianto. In the first half of 2026 MDKA reported a net profit of US$102 million, reversing a US$16 million loss from the same period a year earlier, with consolidated revenue rising 64 % year‑on‑year to US$1.4 billion. EBITDA increased 191 % to US$512 million, driven by stronger nickel and gold operations.

results.title: PT Bursa Efek Indonesia lowers minimum stock price to Rp 1, analysts warn of heightened volatility
results.body: PT Bursa Efek Indonesia (BEI) announced that the minimum price for listed shares will be reduced from Rp 50 to Rp 1 per share, effective 28 September 2026, as part of a revised Full Call Auction (FCA) trading scheme. The amendment also adjusts the Auto Rejection (AR) rules, keeping a 15 % Auto Rejection Bottom (ARB) for stocks above Rp 10 until 31 December 2026 and setting both Auto Rejection Top (ARA) and ARB at Rp 1 for stocks priced between Rp 1 and Rp 10. From 1 January 2027 the ARB will operate symmetrically across the new price range, providing broader price movement flexibility. Analysts from Indo Premier Sekuritas and BRI Danareksa Sekuritas noted that while the change may improve price discovery and liquidity, it could also increase volatility for low‑priced, thinly traded stocks.

results.title: PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (ADRO) highlighted as a cheap big‑cap stock linked to Boy Thohir
results.body: The article spotlights PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (ADRO) as a low‑priced big‑cap stock associated with Garibaldi “Boy” Thohir. It notes a trailing‑twelve‑months PE of 7.6× and a closing price of Rp 2,600 on 25 September 2026, with the share up 1.5% that day but down 1.5% over the prior week and 1.1% over the month, while YTD performance rose 43.6%. Financially, ADRO reported H1‑2026 revenue of US$999 million (+16.5% YoY), EBITDA of US$491 million (+56.8% YoY) and net profit of US$309 million (+76.9% YoY). The article also records a foreign net‑sell of Rp 78.3 billion during the week of 21‑25 September 2026 and identifies Garibaldi Thohir, Christian Ariano Rachmat, Michael WP Soeryadjaya and Arini Saraswaty Subianto as the individual beneficial owners of ADRO.

results.title: Popular news roundup: Fore Coffee expansion, GOTO price‑floor removal, FCA board changes, MBMA profit surge and CDIA IPO fund use
results.body: PT Fore Kopi Indonesia Tbk (FORE) reported that its Fore Coffee brand now operates over 360 stores in Indonesia and Singapore, while PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO) saw the Bursa Efek Indonesia lift the Rp50 price floor to Rp1 effective 28 September 2026, ending its prolonged “gocap” status. In the same roundup, PT Merdeka Battery Materials Tbk (MBMA) posted a net profit of US$54 million for H1‑2026, an 830% year‑on‑year increase, and PT Chandra Daya Investasi Tbk (CDIA) disclosed that 78.45% (Rp1.8 trillion) of its IPO proceeds had been utilized, leaving Rp511 billion unspent.

results.title: PT GMF Aero Asia Tbk (GMFI) posts 23% net profit rise in H1 2026 as quasi‑reorganization fuels 57% stock upside outlook
results.body: The article reports that PT GMF Aero Asia Tbk (GMFI) delivered solid H1 2026 results, with net profit up 23% to US$10.8 million. Revenue rose 51% to US$270.3 million, driven by an engine segment jump of 180% to US$89.5 million and operating profit increasing 81% to US$27.8 million, though net profit was moderated by higher pre‑EBIT expenses. BRI Danareksa Sekuritas estimates the quasi‑reorganization could lift GMFI’s share price by about 57%, noting that H1 revenue already represents half of its full‑year projection and that global MRO spending of US$140 billion in 2026, growing 3.3% annually, offers a favorable backdrop, especially as engine maintenance accounts for 48% of domestic demand. The outlook assumes seasonal factors will keep net profit in line with expectations.

results.title: Foreign investors dump these stocks over the week as the IDX Composite falls 3.09% to 6,241.89
results.body: The article reports that foreign investors sold large amounts of shares in ten listed companies during the week when the IDX Composite (IHSG) fell 3.09% to 6,241.89 points. Over the week, foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp 4.39 trillion across the market, with a further Rp 559.07 billion sold on Friday alone. The ten most heavily net‑sold stocks were PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (MDKA) (Rp 149.63 billion), PT Bumi Resources Minerals Tbk (BRMS) (Rp 82.11 billion), PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk (AADI) (Rp 79.98 billion), PT Triputra Agro Persada Tbk (TAPG) (Rp 67.23 billion), PT Indokripto Koin Semesta Tbk (COIN) (Rp 48.70 billion), PT VKTR Teknologi Mobilitas Tbk (VKTR) (Rp 44.98 billion), PT Erajaya Swasembada Tbk (ERAA) (Rp 35.61 billion), PT Vale Indonesia Tbk (INCO) (Rp 29.44 billion), PT Singaraja Putra Tbk (SINI) (Rp 28.42 billion) and PT Barito Renewables Energy Tbk (BREN) (Rp 18.91 billion). These companies, representing large‑cap and sector‑diverse issuers, were the primary targets of the foreign sell‑off, while other large‑cap stocks, including banks, saw mixed activity with some foreign accumulation. The concentration of foreign selling on these ten issuers contributed to the overall downward pressure on the IHSG during the week.

results.title: Foreign investors net sold Rp 4.39 trillion this week, with banks leading the top‑selling stocks
results.body: Foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp 4.39 trillion across the market during the week ending 26/9/2026, contributing to the IHSG’s 3.09% decline to 6,241.89 points. The ten most net‑sold stocks were PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) Rp 1.1 trillion, PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) Rp 676.34 billion, PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) Rp 597.42 billion, PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (TLKM) Rp 478.55 billion, PT Amman Mineral Internasional Tbk (AMMN) Rp 213.79 billion, PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (ADRO) Rp 159.15 billion, PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (BBNI) Rp 125.58 billion, PT Bayan Resources Tbk (BYAN) Rp 96.45 billion, PT Barito Pacific Tbk (BRPT) Rp 74.93 billion and PT Indosat Tbk (ISAT) Rp 72.91 billion.

results.title: United Tractors' long journey toward a sustainable industry
results.body: United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) is pursuing a transformation to balance its coal and non‑coal businesses to 50:50 by 2030 and cut greenhouse‑gas emissions 30% by that year. The company is optimizing its core through subsidiary PT Pamapersada Nusantara (PAMA), which has adopted ERP S/4HANA and Mine Image Recognition, while diversifying into nickel via subsidiary PT Danusa Tambang Nusantara (DTN) smelter and gold via subsidiary PT Agincourt Resources (PTAR) with biodiversity‑focused ESG due diligence. Renewable‑energy efforts are channeled through subsidiary PT Energi Prima Nusantara (EPN), which holds a 31.49% stake in PT Arkora Hydro Tbk (ARKO) operating 27.4 MW of hydro capacity and 15.4 MW under construction, alongside floating solar projects, geothermal exploration via PT Supreme Energy Rantau Dedap (SERD) and waste‑to‑energy partnerships. Up to 30 June 2026, UNTR reported net revenue of Rp58.28 trillion and net profit of Rp956 billion, with segment revenues of Rp14.97 trillion (heavy equipment), Rp27.16 trillion (mining contractor), Rp12.86 trillion (thermal & metallurgical coal) and Rp2.35 trillion (non‑coal mineral mining); emissions intensity fell to 12.03% in 2025 and renewable‑energy consumption rose to 23.99 million GJ, including 15,298.56 GJ from solar.

results.title: PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (MDKA) reports US$102 million net profit for H1 2026, reversing US$16 million loss
results.body: PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (MDKA) posted a net profit attributable to the parent of US$102 million in the first half of 2026, up from a loss of US$16 million in the same period a year earlier. Consolidated revenue rose 64 percent year‑on‑year to US$1.40 billion and EBITDA surged 191 percent to US$512 million. The turnaround was driven by strong performance of its subsidiaries, with PT Merdeka Battery Materials Tbk (MBMA) remaining the largest contributor to MDKA’s EBITDA through higher nickel ore production (15.2 million wmt, up 121 %) and sales, while PT Merdeka Gold Resources Tbk (EMAS) boosted earnings with a 32 percent increase in gold output to 66,814 ounces. The group also highlighted progress on strategic projects such as the Tujuh Bukit copper feasibility study and expansion of the Pani gold mine, supporting long‑term value creation.

results.title: Second Liner Stocks Remain Prospective Through End‑2026, Catalysts Highlighted
results.body: The article discusses that second‑liner equities are still viewed as having upside potential up to the end of 2026, supported by specific catalysts. Index data as of 25 September 2026 show the IDX SMC Composite down 21.80 % YTD and IDX SMC Liquid down 16.29 % YTD, outperforming the broader IHSG which fell 27.81 % YTD. Analysts point to sector exposure and company‑specific drivers for PT Bumi Resources Minerals Tbk (BRMS), PT Darma Henwa Tbk (DEWA) and PT Sawit Sumbermas Sarana Tbk (SSMS) as examples of second‑liner stocks with growth catalysts such as increased mining production, operating‑earnings inflection and high CPO prices. Additional buy recommendations include AKRA, DSNG, SSMS and TAPG with target prices of Rp 1,800, Rp 1,760, Rp 2,000 and Rp 2,050 respectively. Risks noted are high interest rates, rupiah and oil volatility, foreign outflows and execution risk.

results.title: PT Sinar Mas Agro Resources and Technology Tbk (SMAR) prepares Rp958 billion to repay maturing 2021 Sustainable Bond
results.body: PT Sinar Mas Agro Resources and Technology Tbk (SMAR) has set aside Rp958 billion to settle the principal of its Sustainable Bond III SMART Phase II 2021 Series C that matures on 19 Oct 2026. The company says its healthy liquidity position, confirmed by consolidated financial statements as of 30 June 2026, enables the scheduled repayment, with the funds to be transferred to the account of PT Kustodian Sentral Efek Indonesia (KSEI). SMAR’s latest financial results show net sales of Rp43.73 trillion (up 1.08% YoY), net profit of Rp2.34 trillion (up 185.36% YoY), and gross profit of Rp6.93 trillion (up 58.94% YoY), while cost of goods sold fell to Rp36.8 trillion. PEFINDO maintained SMAR’s credit rating at idAA- with a stable outlook, and the company still has additional sustainable bonds due in 2027, 2031 and 2033.

results.title: PT Golden Plantation Tbk (GOLL) placed under special monitoring by BEI due to revenue shortfall and subsidiary legal issues
results.body: PT Golden Plantation Tbk (GOLL) has been moved to the Indonesia Stock Exchange’s Special Monitoring List. The status became effective on 26 September 2026, as announced by PT Bursa Efek Indonesia (BEI). BEI cited criteria number 3, indicating no revenue or no change in revenue in the latest financial statements, and criteria number 9, relating to a material‑revenue‑contributing subsidiary of GOLL that is under PKPU or bankruptcy proceedings. The special monitoring aims to provide greater investor protection and transparency while urging stakeholders to watch GOLL’s operational and financial developments.

results.title: PT Sarimelati Kencana Tbk (PZZA) reports lower H1 2026 revenue and profit despite modest store expansion
results.body: PT Sarimelati Kencana Tbk (PZZA), the operator of Pizza Hut in Indonesia, posted a decline in first‑half 2026 revenue to Rp 1.47 trillion from Rp 1.54 trillion a year earlier. Operating profit fell to Rp 24.44 billion and net profit to Rp 8.27 billion, compared with Rp 40.61 billion and Rp 15.56 billion respectively in the same period of 2025. The company increased its store base to 579 outlets and reduced its workforce to 4,085 employees as of 30 June 2026, and paid a dividend of Rp 5 billion (Rp 1.66 per share) on 3 June 2026. PT Sarimelati Kencana Tbk (PZZA) remains controlled by PT Sriboga Raturaya, which holds 64.79 % of the shares.

results.title: PT Asuransi Harta Aman Pratama Tbk (AHAP) Receives OJK Approval for Rights Issue
results.body: PT Asuransi Harta Aman Pratama Tbk (AHAP) obtained an effective approval from OJK on 28 September 2026 for its Rights Issue (PMHMETD V). The issue allows up to 3.5 billion new shares at a nominal price of Rp50 per share, potentially raising Rp175 billion, with each holder of seven existing shares entitled to five rights. PT Asuransi Central Asia (ACA), the principal shareholder of AHAP, will subscribe to the full allocation of 2,190,245,006 new shares (62.58% of the issue), converting a Rp30 billion subordinated loan into capital and paying the remaining Rp79.51 billion in cash. The new shares will be listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange on 12 October 2026, with trading, subscription, and payment periods running from 12 to 16 October and related cum‑/ex‑HMETD dates set in early October.

results.title: PT Merdeka Battery Materials Tbk (MBMA) reports net profit of US$54 million in H1 2026, up 830% YoY
results.body: The issuer PT Merdeka Battery Materials Tbk (MBMA) posted net profit of US$54 million in the first half of 2026, an 830% increase from the same period in 2025. Revenue rose 67% to US$1.05 billion and EBITDA climbed 306% to US$311 million, driven by higher nickel ore production (15.2 million wet metric tonnes, up 121%) and sales (12.4 million wet metric tonnes, up 60%), as well as growth in Nickel Pig Iron and High‑Grade Nickel Matte output. The company attributed the performance to expanded mining volume, improved processing, and a new pricing formula for nickel ore, while noting ongoing ramp‑up of related assets such as PT Merdeka Tsingshan Indonesia’s acid operations, PT ESG New Energy Material’s MHP production, and the commissioning of PT Sulawesi Nickel Cobalt.

results.title: PT Antam (Persero) Tbk (Antam) absorbs 9 tons of gold from PT Freeport Indonesia through August 2026
results.body: PT Antam (Persero) Tbk (Antam) has purchased nine tons of gold from PT Freeport Indonesia (PTFI) between January and August 2026 as part of its effort to strengthen the domestic gold supply chain. The transaction builds on an existing gold trade agreement of up to 30 tons per year and complements Antam’s collaborations with several Indonesian gold producers such as PT Amman Mineral Nusa Tenggara (AMNT), PT Citra Palu Minerals (CPM), PT Agincourt Resources, PT Sumbawa Jutaraya (SJR), PT J Resources Bolaang Mongondow (JRBM) and PT Indo Muro Kencana (IMK). In the first half of 2026 Antam reported gold sales of 18,080 kg (18.08 tons) worth Rp50.39 trillion, a 1 % increase YoY, contributing roughly 80 % of its total net sales of Rp62.71 trillion, while its own mine production amounted to 433 kg.

results.title: PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (MDKA) posts H1 2026 net profit of US$102 million
results.body: PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (MDKA) posted a net profit attributable to owners of the parent of US$102 million for the first half of 2026, reversing a US$16 million loss a year earlier, as nickel and gold businesses strengthened. Consolidated revenue grew 64% year‑on‑year to US$1.40 billion and EBITDA surged 191% to US$512 million. The nickel segment, operating through PT Merdeka Battery Materials Tbk (MBMA), lifted production 121% to 15.2 million wet metric tonnes and sales 60% to 12.4 million wmt, while gold output rose 32% to 66,814 ounces, driven by Tambang Emas Tujuh Bukit and the newly commissioned Tambang Emas Pani. PT ESG New Energy Material expanded Mixed Hydroxide Precipitate output and PT Sulawesi Nickel Cobalt progressed its High Pressure Acid Leach project, as MDKA pursues further growth projects and monitors commodity prices, energy costs, exchange rates and regulatory developments.

results.title: Asuransi Harta Aman Pratama (AHAP) launches Rp175 billion right issue, with PT Asuransi Central Asia subscribing Rp109.51 billion
results.body: AHAP announced a right issue of Rp175 billion, issuing 3.5 billion new shares at a nominal price of Rp50 each. PT Asuransi Central Asia, the main shareholder of AHAP owned by Anthoni Salim, will subscribe to 2.19 billion shares (62.58% of the new issue) representing a nominal value of Rp109.51 billion, funded by a Rp30 billion subordinated loan conversion and Rp79.51 billion cash. The proceeds will be used to satisfy POJK No.23/2023 equity requirements of at least Rp250 billion by 31 December 2026 and for working‑capital investments, with non‑exercising shareholders facing up to 41.67% dilution. The right‑issue timeline sets cum‑right from 6‑8 October 2026, ex‑right on 7‑9 October, recording on 8 October, distribution on 9 October, and listing on the Indonesia Stock Exchange on 12 October 2026.

results.title: Merdeka Battery (MBMA) reports 830% profit surge to USD54.43 million in H1 2026
results.body: Merdeka Battery (MBMA) posted a net profit of USD54.43 million for the first half of 2026, an increase of 830.42% compared with USD5.85 million a year earlier. Revenue rose 66.66% to USD1.05 billion, while cost of goods sold grew to USD773.63 million, resulting in gross profit of USD274.13 million and operating profit of USD251.48 million. Earnings per share on a basic and diluted basis increased to USD0,00050 from USD0,00005, and profit for the period reached USD149.42 million, up from USD28.51 million. The company’s balance sheet expanded, with total assets reaching USD4.24 billion, equity USD2.47 billion, and liabilities USD1.77 billion at the end of the period.

results.title: Bank Central Asia (PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA)) stock again draws investor focus
results.body: PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) saw a foreign net buy of Rp 103.17 billion on 25 September 2026, lifting the share price 0.40% to Rp 6,250 with a volume of 89.45 million shares. UOB Kay Hian Sekuritas maintained a buy rating, setting a target price of Rp 8,150 (≈30% upside) and citing solid funding, capital and liquidity, while reporting August 2026 net profit of Rp 4.92 trillion (+13.1% YoY) and forecasting 2026‑2027 profits of Rp 60 trillion and Rp 65 trillion with dividend yields of 5.7% and 6.1%. The bank also refuted social‑media rumors of an acquisition by Andi Syamsuddin Arsyad (Haji Isam), confirming no corporate action plans.

results.title: Merdeka (MDKA) reports USD101.8 million net profit in 2026, a 743% surge from last year’s loss
results.body: Merdeka (MDKA), the "emiten asuhan Boy Thohir" mentioned in the article, posted a net profit of USD101.8 million for 2026, reversing a USD15.8 million loss from the prior year. Basic earnings per share rose to USD0,0042 from a negative USD0,0006. Revenue climbed 64.7% to USD1.4 billion, with gross profit increasing to USD433.94 million and operating profit to USD397.29 million. Total equity reached USD3.09 billion, assets USD6.46 billion, and the shares rose 0.33% to Rp3,070, lifting the market capitalization to Rp75.13 trillion.

results.title: BEI removes Rp 50 floor price, opening trading range for PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO)
results.body: The Indonesia Stock Exchange will eliminate the Rp 50 minimum price floor for all listed securities, effective 28 September 2026, directly affecting PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO) which has been stuck at that level since 5 May 2026. The sell‑order queue at the Rp 50 price reached 394,120,672 lots, valued at roughly Rp 1.97 trillion as of 25 September 2026. MNC Sekuritas analyst Christian noted that the removal may allow GOTO’s price to fall below Rp 50 in the short term but should reduce trading barriers and improve liquidity and price discovery. BEI Director‑General Jeffrey Hendrik said the change is expected to boost liquidity and provide better price discovery for previously stagnant stocks such as GOTO.

results.title: Indonesia’s capital market raises Rp147 trillion, with EBUS contributing Rp128.81 trillion
results.body: The article reports that Indonesia’s capital market has raised about Rp147 trillion up to 25 September 2026. Bursa Efek Indonesia (BEI) records that the bulk of the funds, Rp128.81 trillion, came from debt and sukuk issuances (EBUS). Rights issues contributed Rp16.23 trillion and initial public offerings added Rp2.16 trillion, with seven companies already listed and six more in the IPO pipeline. BEI also notes 132 EBUS issuances from 62 issuers and 22 pending issuances from 16 issuers, with the financial sector leading the pipeline.
